title: OrionFleet prospect signal map and outbound play
content:
Topline/Intent:
- Quick brainstorm notes for outbound + initial research on OrionFleet (mid-market logistics/3PL). They have ~420 drivers, regional hubs in SE and Midwest, pilotable use cases: customer messaging, routing decisions (heuristics -> ML), and claims triage.

Why this could be a fit (signals):
- Public job postings: "Senior Site Reliability Engineer (edge systems)" – signals investment in real-time infra.
- Customer emails leaked in forum threads complaining about late arrival notifications -> potential to automate timely, human-sounding updates with low-latency hosted agents.
- Tech stack mentions Kafka + k8s + AWS (us-east) -> we can propose Redwood Private in their VPC or a dedicated region setup.
- Looking at their investor deck: EBITDA-sensitive, cost per route matters; talk to Redwood Optimize first (batching + quantization recommendations).

Primary stakeholders (who to target):
- Ops/Platform: Maia Thompson, Head of Platform (likely champion for latency/cost controls)
- Head of Customer Experience: James Osei (owns driver->customer comms)
- CTO: Victor Huang (strategic buy-in, security)
- Vendor procurement/security: Dalia Reed (will push for KMS/HSM + SOC2)

Champion profile & angle:
- Maia (Platform): cares about predictable tail latency and deterministic failover. Pitch: Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput + can set routing policies to fail to cheaper variants. Emphasize dev ergonomics + SDKs for quick integration.
- James (CX): cares about higher conversion for ETA messages and fewer CS tickets. Pitch: Redwood hosted API for fast PoC with NLU-powered status messages and A/B evals to measure CS ticket lift.

Concrete use cases to propose in outreach call:
1) ETA and proactive messaging: replace templated SMS with Redwood chat generation + structured output for template fields. Measure reduction in inbound CS volume.
2) Claims triage assistant: ingest driver photos + description -> generate first-line claim summary + severity tags for human reviewer. Could be Private for PII.
3) Route exception rerouting helper: embed model to summarize driver notes and suggest reroute options; integrate with their tasking admin.

Metrics to highlight in pitch (numbers to use carefully):
- Latency: 95th p99 target < 350ms for short messages (benchmark with our hosted small-model profile).
- Cost: show sample delta: batch+quantization -> 30–50% token cost reduction vs vanilla hosting.
- Business impact: target 12–18% reduction in CS ticket volume from better messaging in a 90-day pilot.

Objections we should be ready for and suggested responses:
- "We can't send data off-prem / sensitive PII": Offer Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). Explain KMS integrations and audit logs; propose initial PoC with redacted PHI to prove flows.
- "Latency won't be predictable at scale": Recommend Dedicated reserved capacity; show routing policy fallback and autoscaling profile. Offer synthetic load test with their sample traces.
- "Costs will balloon": Provide Redwood Optimize report sample + pay-as-you-go hosted PoC with strict quota + cost dashboard. Show batching strategy and inference profiles that cap cost.
- "Integration work is too heavy": Share simple SDK example + 4–6 week scoping with Solutions Eng. Offer runbook and prebuilt webhook consumer for their stack.

Initial outreach cadence (lean, 6 touches):
T1 (email, short): 1–2 lines hook referencing a specific pain (ETA complaints) + ask for 20m. Subject: "Quick idea to reduce OrionFleet ETA tickets by X%"
T2 (LinkedIn + 1-line follow-up): call out mutual investor or region hub.
T3 (value email): 2 bullets: pilot scope + timeline + a one-pager link.
T4 (call attempt + voicemail): reference prior notes, offer calendar window.
T5 (if no response): share a short recording (2–3 min) demoing a sample generated ETA message + metrics.
T6 (breakup): keep warm; offer to re-engage after Q2 planning.

Draft email (first outreach) - keep short, test subject lines: 
Subject options:
- "Idea: lower OrionFleet ETA tickets in 90 days"
- "Prototype: human-sounding ETA updates for OrionFleet customers"

Body draft:
Hey Maia —
Small idea from reviewing some public posts & the OrionFleet careers page: customers are frequently pinging CS about ETAs and drivers spend time manually updating routed stops. We built a quick approach at Redwood that: 1) generates short, personalized ETA messages, 2) produces structured fields you can insert into existing SMS templates, and 3) runs with predictable latency.
Would you be up for a 20-min call next week to see a 2-minute demo and discuss a lightweight pilot (4 hubs)? I can share a one-pager + cost-estimate.
— Samira

What to bring to discovery call:
- Sample ETAs and typical message variations (ask for 100 recent message pairs if possible)
- Traffic profile (tokens per message, concurrent messages per hub)
- Security checklist (do they need Private? what certs?)
- Success criteria: % CS reduction target, latency SLOs, and cost guardrails

Technical quicknotes for Solutions Eng pairing:
- Recommend starting model family: small to medium LLM (quantized) on dedicated nodes for pilot; fallback to smaller hosted family during spike.
- Integration sketch: inbound event -> pinned prompt template + structured JSON output -> templating engine -> SMS provider. Track token usage per template.
- Observability: enable per-route token/latency dashboards + rollout canary on a subset of hubs.

Risks / unknowns to validate early:
- How many SMS providers do they use? (Twillio vs vendor)
- Do drivers have app-based message suppression rules?
- Legal/regulatory: are there clauses in carrier agreements about automated messages?

Next actions (my checklist):
- [ ] Pull 100 public/cleared ETA samples (ask James) — due 3/12
- [ ] Spin up Redwood hosted demo with canned data — due 3/16
- [ ] Draft one-pager (cost + pilot timeline) — due 3/14 (Diego to review)
- [ ] Schedule intro to Solutions Eng (Priya) once Maia replies

Notes to self:
- Keep pitch low-friction: start with hosted PoC for messaging only; escalate to Private for claims triage.
- Emphasize measurable guardrails (cost dashboard + token limits) because finance will push back.
- If Maia is skeptical on latency, offer synthetic replay using their Kafka traces (ask for 24-hour sample).

End of scratchpad.

Random ideas to test in A/B for messages:
- Include ETA + confidence band ("arriving ~3:45–4:00pm") vs fixed time
- Add micro-personalization: driver first name or vehicle color when available
- Offer an opt-in link to live-tracking when ETA variance > 12 minutes

-- Samira (notes, will iterate after discovery)
